Macrons

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Body, health & movement

fever noun

also temperature, have a temperature, run a fever, hot forehead

classical

Traupman 64
M-O s.v. fever
Traupman 55: frōns et genae sunt calidae

1febris: e left unmarked (Lewis & Short fē^bris, marking the e as common, “the ē predominating in poets”). The poets’ long scansion may only reflect the heavy syllable before -br-, and de Vaan (s.v. febris) does not discuss the quantity.

febris1, febris f.

noun, third declension

Accusative febrim or febrem.

Other words

  • febrīcula, febrīculae f. — a slight temperature

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 12.1.2, of his little daughter Attica: dē Atticae febrīculā … valdē doluī

    Long ī (L&S).

  • febrīcitāre — run a fever

    also used · classical · Traupman 64; Cels., post-Augustan

    Long ī (L&S).

Examples

  • febrim habēre

    have a feverCic. Fam. 7.26.1

  • in febrim incidere

    get a feverCic. Fam. 14.8.1

  • Frōns calida est.

    Your forehead is hot.composed

  • Febrim habēs; hodiē domī manēbimus.

    You’ve got a temperature; we’ll stay home today.composed

See also ill, shiver, forehead.

SourcesLewis & Short: febris · Lewis & Short: febricula · Lewis & Short: febricito

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. fever. John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): pp. 55, 64.

Cicero’s letters checked against the Perseus Latin texts.
